items.title: Gigaphoton debuts neon recycling system with claimed 50% recovery rate
items.description: New neon gas recycling systems promise to reduce the demand for the noble gas at major chip manufacturers using DUV lithography. But as that technology is supplanted, this much-needed fix may only be needed temporarily.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Japanese semiconductor lithography tool maker Gigaphoton has developed a novel neon gas recycling system named hTGM for its argon fluoride (ArF) excimer lasers. The method has demonstrated a 50% recycling rate, with hopes that it can be improved dramatically with adjusted configurations, Business Wire reports. This could help fill a gap in the chip supply chain caused by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Before 2022, Ukraine shipped up to 50% of the neon gas used in the semiconductor industry, but its major producers had to stop exports, raising concerns over chip supply. 70% of global neon production is used in semiconductor manufacturing, particularly in advanced DUV processes.In the aftermath, China, Taiwan, and South Korea all increased their own domestic Neon production efforts, but various chip manufacturers also integrated recycling systems at various points during the fabrication process. Gigaphoton's more efficient ArF lasers with neon recycling could further help close those loops, reducing material costs and further reducing reliance on global supply chains.It's not the only company pushing this technology forward, either. At the start of September, Japanese environmental protection company Kanken Techno demonstrated its own Neon gas recycling system for excimer lasers at SemiCon Taiwan. It demonstrated a recycling rate of over 90%, suggesting there is considerable headroom to improve this process in the future.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: What makes Neon so scarce?Neon is one of a handful of noble gases, making it inert under standard conditions and easy to handle. However, the ease with which it vaporizes and its limited bonding ability mean it is relatively scarce in Earth's atmosphere, making it scarce. It is most efficiently obtained through fractional distillation of super-cooled air, making it most affordable to obtain as a byproduct of other processes. For decades, Ukrainian steel-mill air-separation units produced crude neon from large-scale air-separation units (ASUs), and then refined it in-country via a pair of key companies.That meant that when Russia escalated its war against Ukraine into a full-scale invasion in 2022 and Ukrainian neon refiners shut down production, there was an immediate global response. You may like Lumentum CEO warns of impending bottleneck on critical material used for silicon photonics China's DUV technology 'at a similar stage to ASML in 2004,' analyst claims ASML says it sold 'absolutely nothing' in Europe in 2026 As SFA Oxford explains, South Korea accelerated domestic production and implemented a large-scale, national neon recycling initiative focused on in-fab recovery. Taiwan installed purification systems in existing blast-furnace ASUs, developing its own domestic supply chain. By utilizing its national infrastructure, it targeted complete self-sufficiency in neon gas production within a few years.China integrated neon gas purification into many elements of its industrial base, twinning it with steel and petrochemical production facilities. The U.S. also responded with the development of new ASUs at Gulf-coast petrochemical hubs, but those aren't expected to meaningfully improve American neon supplies until near the end of the decade.Lithography accounts for around 70% of global neon use, particularly in more advanced DUV processes — though crucially, not in EUV lithography, which uses a tin-plasma laser instead. With global DUV-produced semiconductor supply rapidly advancing in the wake of the AI buildout, neon supply is an important component in the chip supply chain, which has rapidly evolved to become a key asset within strategic defence and global trade.Working with what you've gotFor individual companies that can't directly control their supply chains, recycling has been a much more immediate focus. The first neon gas recycling systems were qualified for use with Cymer excimer ArF lasers at the end of 2023, and Samsung and SK Hynix became the first of the major memory makers to implement neon gas recycling in 2024.Gigaphoton previously offered neon recycling with KrF (krypton fluoride) lasers, but has now extended that recycling capability to ArF lasers as well. It claims a single hTGM for ArF unit can reduce neon gas consumption by up to 470 kilotres per year, representing substantial material cost savings, as well as reducing company reliance on a global supply chain that has been sufficiently unstable in recent years. What to read next Analyst firm says ASML unlikely to back particle accelerator chipmaking tech Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined — Beijing's nascent lithography tools target DUV production at five machines a year, and an EUV prototype with no chips China stockpiled 343 immersion DUV tools for advanced chipmaking However, its claims of a 50% recycling rate aren't exactly groundbreaking. Cymer's excimer laser neon recovery system demonstrated that same level of efficiency in 2015, and Gigaphoton's own testing suggested a potential peak for ArF recovery of over 90% in 2017.That suggests it should be able to ramp up its efforts to a higher percentage quite swiftly. Especially since fellow Japanese firm Kanken Techno recently unveiled a neon recycling system with over 90% efficiency. Kanken works with both major ArF laser developers and is currently going through the certification process, with expected approval in the near future.A temporary fix?With neon gas recycling during chip production effectively solved, it may be that the supply of neon for the chip industry has proved to be a temporary problem. But it may be a temporary solution too, as the use of neon within the industry may be set to shrink dramatically in the years to come.EUV lithography can build far more complex chips than DUV, and offers a future path beyond the need for neon gas usage in excimer lasers as newer electronics adopt the more capable chip designs. On top of that, alternative technologies to DUV are being developed which could produce the same DUV light to generate advanced semiconductors, but without the need for noble or toxic gases.Solid-state laser technologies have been rapidly developing in recent years, though last year's Chinese efforts are still below required industrial power thresholds. Nanoimprint lithography also holds promise as a DUV alternative, as well as cutting costs by a comparative 90%.There are still huge hurdles in performance and certification, as well as integration with existing fabrication plans and supply chains. But the potential to move beyond the need for neon gas within semiconductor lithography is there. Over the coming years, the combination of laser neon recycling systems and alternative manufacturing techniques could reduce the need for international neon sources to a fraction of existing levels.

items.titleZh: Gigaphoton推出氖气回收系统，声称回收率达50%
items.descriptionZh:
日本半导体光刻工具制造商 Gigaphoton 开发出名为 hTGM 的新型氖气回收系统，用于氩氟（ArF）准分子激光器。该系统已实现 50% 的氖气回收率，公司希望调整配置后大幅提升。Business Wire 报道称，这有助于填补俄乌战争造成的芯片供应链缺口。2022 年前，乌克兰供应半导体行业最多 50% 的氖气，但其主要生产商停止出口，引发芯片供应担忧。全球约 70% 的氖气产量用于半导体制造，尤其先进 DUV 工艺。此后，中国大陆、中国台湾地区和韩国均加大本土氖气生产，芯片制造商也在制造环节整合回收系统。Gigaphoton 为 ArF 激光加入氖回收，可进一步形成闭环，降低材料成本和对全球供应链的依赖。与此同时，日本环保企业 Kanken Techno 也在 9 月初 SEMICON Taiwan 展示了用于准分子激光的氖回收系统，回收率超过 90%，显示该工艺仍有很大提升空间。

氖是惰性气体，标准条件下不易反应、易于处理，但容易挥发且键合能力有限，在地球大气中相对稀缺。最有效的获取方式是对超冷空气进行分馏，而作为其他工业过程的副产品获取最为经济。几十年来，乌克兰钢厂的大型空气分离装置（ASU）生产粗氖，再由两家关键公司在本国精炼。2022 年俄乌冲突全面升级后，乌克兰氖精炼商停产，全球随即作出反应。韩国加速国内生产，并实施大规模国家氖回收倡议，重点放在晶圆厂内回收；中国台湾地区在现有高炉 ASU 中安装净化系统，发展本土供应链，目标是在几年内实现氖气完全自给；中国大陆将氖气净化整合进钢铁、石化等工业基础；美国则在墨西哥湾沿岸石化中心开发新 ASU，但预计到本十年末才能明显改善美国氖供应。光刻是氖的主要用途之一，尤其在先进 DUV 工艺中，但 EUV 不使用氖，而是使用锡等离子激光。随着 AI 建设推动 DUV 半导体供应，氖供应已成为芯片供应链以及战略防务和全球贸易中的关键资产。

对无法直接控制供应链的企业而言，回收是更直接的应对方式。首批氖回收系统于 2023 年底获准用于 Cymer 准分子 ArF 激光器，三星和 SK 海力士则在 2024 年成为首批实施氖回收的主要存储制造商。Gigaphoton 此前已为 KrF 激光提供氖回收，如今将能力扩展到 ArF。公司声称，单个用于 ArF 的 hTGM 单元每年最多可减少 470 千单位（原文写作 kilotres）的氖气消耗，带来可观的物料成本节省，并降低对近年不稳定全球供应链的依赖。不过，50% 的回收率并非突破性水平：Cymer 的准分子激光氖回收系统在 2015 年就展示过同等效率，Gigaphoton 自己在 2017 年的测试也显示 ArF 回收潜在峰值可超过 90%。这意味着其回收率应能较快提升，尤其 Kanken Techno 最近已推出效率超过 90% 的氖回收系统。Kanken 与主要 ArF 激光开发商合作，目前正进行认证，预计不久后获批。

从未来看，芯片生产中的氖回收已有效解决，氖供应可能只是暂时问题，但回收也可能只是临时方案，因为氖在半导体行业中的使用量可能大幅缩小。EUV 能制造比 DUV 更复杂的芯片，随着新电子设备采用更先进设计，未来路径可能超越准分子激光对氖的需求。此外，替代 DUV 的技术正在开发，可产生相同 DUV 光来制造先进半导体，却无需稀有或有毒气体。固态激光技术近年发展迅速，但中国去年的相关努力仍低于工业功率阈值；纳米压印光刻也有望替代 DUV，并相对降低约 90% 成本。这些方案在性能、认证以及与现有晶圆厂和供应链整合方面仍有巨大障碍，但摆脱半导体光刻对氖气依赖的潜力已经存在。未来，激光氖回收系统与替代制造技术结合，可能将国际氖源需求降至现有水平的一小部分。

items.title: Why Telecom Operators Are Building Their AI Strategy on Open Models
items.description: Telecom operators are increasingly building their AI strategies on open models — and the reasons go beyond mere cost.  Open models give telcos the ability to trust, control and customize AI across their most critical workloads — from autonomous networks to customer care.  NVIDIA’s latest State of AI in Telecommunications report reflects this shift, with […]
items.content: Telecom operators are increasingly building their AI strategies on open models — and the reasons go beyond mere cost. Open models give telcos the ability to trust, control and customize AI across their most critical workloads — from autonomous networks to customer care. NVIDIA’s latest State of AI in Telecommunications report reflects this shift, with 89% of respondents reporting that open source models and software are important to their company’s AI strategy. For operators, the strategic value of open models is fivefold: They expand access to frontier‑level intelligence at lower cost, allowing operators to reserve closed models for the workloads where they drive the most value. Independent benchmarks such as the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 show that leading open models are becoming more competitive across demanding reasoning, coding, scientific and agentic workloads. They support telco‑specific customization, with open weights and training recipes that operators can fine‑tune for their own operations using network, customer and industry data. They enable trustworthy AI by giving telcos greater visibility into and control over model artifacts and behavior, so models can be evaluated, adapted and governed in alignment with regulations and business policies. They enable flexible, secure deployment: teams can size and optimize open models to run across public clouds, private infrastructure and edge environments. They unlock the opportunity for telcos to deliver locally adapted AI services to enterprise and government customers by hosting and fine-tuning open models. Open Foundations, Tuned for Telecom Operations The NVIDIA Nemotron family of open models provides frontier-level reasoning performance optimized for agentic workflows, as well as speech capabilities for voice applications, with open weights, training data and recipes. SoftBank Corp. illustrates how an operator can use open models as a basis for developing and continuously advancing its telecom-specific AI capabilities. “Open models allow SoftBank Corp. to build on the rapid progress of global foundation models while applying the network knowledge and operational expertise we have accumulated over many years,” said Rajeev Koodli, principal fellow of SoftBank Corp. and senior vice president of SB Telecom America. “We are using open foundations extensively, including NVIDIA Nemotron models and others, in developing our SoftBank Large Telecom Model, continuously advancing it for telecom-specific use cases such as network operations, design and overall management.” In addition, NVIDIA is collaborating with partners to help turn open models into practical building blocks for telecom AI. NVIDIA announced the 30-billion-parameter Nemotron 3 Large Telco Model (LTM), fine-tuned by AdaptKey on open source telecom datasets to deliver accuracy gains for telecom-specific tasks. This gives operators an open baseline that can understand telecom industry terminology and reason effectively through telecom operations workflows such as network configuration and customer incident triage. To help operators customize the Nemotron 3 LTM and other open models with their own operational data, NVIDIA released the full recipe that walks through the end-to-end fine-tuning pipeline for adapting open models to operator-specific networks, customers and procedures using NVIDIA NeMo open libraries. Scale Open Models Into Production Workflows Open models are a critical building block, but it takes more than models to bring autonomous telecom operations safely into production. For AT&T, the value of model choice lies in making that flexibility operational in alignment with its business priorities. “At AT&T, we believe the future of AI is not about choosing a single model; it’s about intelligently matching every workload to the right combination of performance, cost and control,” said Andy Markus, chief data and AI officer of AT&T. “Open models are essential to that approach, and with NVIDIA, we can bring that model-choice strategy into production with the scale, reliability and governance our business requires.” Operators need pipelines that prepare and protect their data for model fine‑tuning by anonymizing sensitive records and generating privacy‑preserving synthetic datasets. They also need a platform that can turn open models into governed, autonomous agentic workflows. NVIDIA provides that end-to-end platform, powered by NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, and spanning data pipelines, open models, agent orchestration, secure runtimes and simulation. Together with a strong partner ecosystem building at every layer of this platform, telecom operators have a clear path to translate the benefits of open models into production-ready AI workflows. Create a Platform for Local AI Innovation As telecom operators build AI infrastructure aligned with national AI strategies, open models are giving them a foundation to deliver AI services tailored to local languages, industries, regulations and data governance requirements. Operators across countries can fine-tune open models for local-language and industry-specific needs, as well as host open models on their trusted platforms that customers can consume directly or build on with their own data and applications. For Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, one of Indonesia’s largest telecom operators, that means building AI that reflects the country’s own language and culture through its Sahabat-AI family of open source models. “For countries like Indonesia, the value of open models goes beyond access to powerful AI. It is about adapting that intelligence to our own language, culture, data and real-world needs,” said Chirag Sukhadia, chief data and AI officer of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison. “Sahabat-AI puts this into practice, using open models as a foundation to build AI that understands Indonesia and can be developed for local applications. This allows us not only to adopt AI, but to build capabilities around it and enable more Indonesians to create with AI on their own terms.” Learn more about NVIDIA technologies for telecommunications.

items.titleZh: 为何电信运营商基于开放模型构建其AI战略
items.descriptionZh:
电信运营商正越来越多地基于开放模型制定AI战略，原因不只是成本。开放模型让运营商能够在其最关键的业务负载中信任、控制和定制AI，从自治网络到客户服务。NVIDIA最新的《电信行业AI现状》报告反映了这一转变：89%的受访者表示，开源模型和软件对其公司的AI战略很重要。对运营商而言，开放模型的战略价值体现在五个方面：以更低成本获得前沿级智能，从而把闭源模型留给价值最高的负载；支持电信专属定制，运营商可利用开放权重和训练配方，结合网络、客户和行业数据对模型进行微调；实现可信AI，让运营商更清楚地了解并控制模型工件和行为，从而按照监管要求和业务政策评估、调整和治理模型；支持灵活、安全的部署，团队可以调整和优化开放模型，使其运行在公有云、私有基础设施和边缘环境中；解锁新机会，运营商可通过托管和微调开放模型，向企业和政府客户提供本地适配的AI服务。

NVIDIA的Nemotron系列开放模型提供面向智能体工作流优化的前沿级推理性能，以及用于语音应用的语音能力，并开放权重、训练数据和配方。软银公司展示了运营商如何以开放模型为基础，开发和持续提升电信专属AI能力。软银公司首席研究员、SB Telecom America高级副总裁Rajeev Koodli表示，开放模型让软银能够在全球基础模型快速进步的基础上，应用其多年积累的网络知识和运营经验。软银正在广泛使用开放基础模型，包括NVIDIA Nemotron等，来开发其“软银大型电信模型”，并持续推进网络运营、设计和整体管理等电信专属用例。

此外，NVIDIA正与合作伙伴协作，将开放模型转化为电信AI的实用构建模块。NVIDIA发布了300亿参数的Nemotron 3 Large Telco Model（LTM），由AdaptKey基于开源电信数据集微调，可提升电信专属任务的准确性。这为运营商提供了一个开放基线，能够理解电信行业术语，并有效推理网络配置、客户事件分诊等电信运营工作流。为帮助运营商用自身运营数据定制Nemotron 3 LTM和其他开放模型，NVIDIA还发布了完整配方，介绍如何使用NVIDIA NeMo开放库，完成将开放模型适配到运营商特定网络、客户和流程的端到端微调流水线。

将开放模型扩展到生产工作流，仅靠模型还不够，还需要把自治电信运营安全地投入生产。对AT&T而言，模型选择的价值在于将这种灵活性与其业务优先级对齐并投入运营。AT&T首席数据与AI官Andy Markus表示，AI的未来不是选择单一模型，而是智能地将每个工作负载匹配到性能、成本和控制的正确组合；开放模型对这一方法至关重要，借助NVIDIA，AT&T可以按业务所需的规模、可靠性和治理，将模型选择战略投入生产。运营商需要流水线来准备和保护用于模型微调的数据，包括匿名化敏感记录和生成保护隐私的合成数据集；还需要一个平台，将开放模型转化为受治理的自治智能体工作流。NVIDIA提供由NVIDIA AI Enterprise软件和NVIDIA Agent Toolkit支持的端到端平台，覆盖数据流水线、开放模型、智能体编排、安全运行时和仿真。再加上在这一平台各层构建的强大合作伙伴生态，电信运营商已有清晰路径，将开放模型的优势转化为生产级AI工作流。

在电信运营商建设与国家AI战略一致的AI基础设施时，开放模型为其提供了基础，可提供适配本地语言、行业、监管和数据治理要求的AI服务。各国运营商可针对本地语言和行业需求微调开放模型，并在其可信平台上托管开放模型，供客户直接使用，或基于自身数据和应用进行构建。对印尼最大电信运营商之一Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison而言，这意味着通过其开源模型系列Sahabat-AI，构建体现印尼自身语言和文化的AI。Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison首席数据与AI官Chirag Sukhadia表示，对印尼这样的国家，开放模型的价值不只是获得强大AI，而是让智能适配本国语言、文化、数据和现实需求。Sahabat-AI将这一理念付诸实践，以开放模型为基础，构建理解印尼的AI，并可为本地应用开发。这不仅让印尼采用AI，也能围绕AI建设能力，让更多印尼人按自己的方式用AI创造。

items.title: EV charging company plans to deploy 100,000 Nvidia GPUs in pods at its roadside sites across the US
items.description: EV charging firm Xeal plans to use its existing U.S. network to deploy the 'world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity.'
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter EV charging firm Xeal plans to use its existing U.S. network to deploy the “world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity.” The big idea is that it already has 1,600+ locations and 200MW of permitted, installed electrical infrastructure, so it aims to “deploy over 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs” at these sites. Thus it has developed Latient Pods (pictured), with each containing up to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUs. We hope charging location security will be adequate to keep thieves away from these cabinets, as they are probably worth $2M+ each.Nikhil Bharadwaj, co-founder and CEO of Xeal, explained that Latient Pods can deliver inference compute today while new data centers are still being built. “Latient is the fastest way to bring new compute online, tapping already permitted and grid-connected, yet idle energy capacity, located right where it's needed for ultra-low latency, with no water hookup requirements,” highlighted the exec. Grid interconnect is said to be one of the trickiest things for those looking to bring new compute online, but Xeal’s EV charging sites, which “typically operate at less than 10% of permitted capacity,” can deliver processing power via a distributed network across a metropolitan area.An Nvidia rep also praised the upcoming Latient Pod network for being an innovative way to bring low-latency inference closer to users while making better use of infrastructure that has already been built.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: In the rendered image from Xeal, a Latient Pod looks quite a lot like a broadband fiber cabinet that you might have on your street. A pod will boast the following specs/features:Powered by idle EV charging capacityUp to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUsSelf-contained independent cooling, no water hookup requiredQuiet operation at less than 65 dBs (comparable to a washing machine)Fixed rental or ancillary revenue for site ownerAdds up to $1 million in property value for little-to-no investmentAll power bills covered as a tenant pass-throughPotential savings for EV charging customersBuilt to withstand the outdoors, NEMA 4 enclosureInstalled and running in hoursIf Xeal has 1,600+ locations, and one Latient Pod has up to 48 GPUs, its touted purchasing target of 100,000 Nvidia GPUs suggests some sites will have more than a single pod at the location. Or perhaps it intends to build more EV sites, up to nearly 2,100 in total. You may like Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to add another 660,000 AI GPUs this year, nearing a total of 1.44 million in operation Startups want to rent your idle gaming PC for AI tasks Nvidia weighs $250 billion guarantee so OpenAI can lease SoftBank's 10-gigawatt Ohio campus, report claims It claims that the location of its pods around metro areas, a feature dubbed Metro Edge, offers sub-20ms latency, a significant speedup over inference located in a distant data center.We’ve previously reported on EVs and distributed computing, but in a slightly different context. Last year we discussed Elon Musk’s proposal to make use of the untapped asset of the millions of Tesla cars out there. He called it “100 gigawatts of inference” that could be used when the vehicles are “bored.”Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsMeanwhile, we must remember that EV charging stations are already being targeted by thieves. We reported about a ‘plague’ of electric car charger cable thefts driven simply by the copper scrap value of the hefty cables used at the sites. Imagine the security that would be required if/when Latient Pods are deployed, stuffed with extremely expensive GPUs. 48 Blackwell GPUs would be worth around $2,000,000 according to 2024 figures – so surely much more by now.The first Latient Pod will be online by the end of the year, says Xeal. items.titleZh: 电动汽车充电公司计划在全美路边站点部署10万块英伟达GPU算力舱
items.descriptionZh:
美国电动车充电企业Xeal宣布，计划利用其现有的美国充电网络，部署“全球首个使用闲置电动车充电容量的边缘推理计算网络”。Xeal目前拥有1600多个站点，以及200MW已获许可并完成安装的电力基础设施。公司希望在这些站点部署超过10万块NVIDIA GPU，从而把原本利用率不高的充电站电力容量转化为分布式AI推理算力。

为此，Xeal开发了Latient Pod。每个Latient Pod最多可容纳48块NVIDIA Hopper或Blackwell Ultra GPU。从外观上看，它类似街道上的宽带光纤机柜，但内部是高密度AI计算设备。其核心创新在于：不再等待新建大型数据中心和漫长的电网互联，而是直接利用已经并网、已获许可但通常闲置的EV充电站容量。Xeal表示，其充电站点通常只运行在许可容量的不到10%，因此有大量电力可供边缘计算使用。Latient Pod采用自包含独立冷却系统，无需接水，噪音低于65分贝，约等于洗衣机；具备NEMA 4户外防护能力，可在数小时内完成安装并运行。

在性能方面，Xeal将这种分布式布局称为“Metro Edge”，即把推理算力部署在都市区周边，从而提供低于20毫秒的延迟，相比把推理任务放在远端数据中心有显著加速。公司认为，Latient Pod是当前最快把新算力上线的方式之一，因为它利用的是已经许可、已经并网、但尚未充分利用的能源容量，并且位于需要超低延迟服务的地点附近，同时不需要水连接。英伟达方面也称赞该网络是一种创新方式，可以把低延迟推理更靠近用户，并更好利用已有基础设施。

从规模看，如果Xeal拥有1600多个站点，而每个Latient Pod最多支持48块GPU，那么其10万块NVIDIA GPU的采购目标意味着部分站点将部署多个Pod，或者Xeal可能将EV站点扩展到接近2100个。每个Pod的商业模式对站点所有者也有吸引力：可获得固定租金或附加收入，几乎无需投资即可为物业增加最高100万美元价值；电费以租户转嫁方式覆盖；还可能为EV充电客户带来潜在节省。

不过，安全是明显风险。电动车充电站已经频繁成为盗窃目标，尤其是粗大充电电缆因铜材回收价值而遭窃。Latient Pod内装满昂贵GPU，按2024年数据，48块Blackwell GPU价值约200万美元，如今只会更高。因此，部署这些机柜需要足够安保。Xeal表示，第一个Latient Pod将在今年年底前上线。此前也有类似分布式算力设想，例如马斯克曾提出利用闲置特斯拉汽车提供“100吉瓦推理”算力，但Xeal的方案是把GPU直接部署在现有EV充电基础设施中，面向都市边缘推理市场。

items.title: Qualcomm will pay Huawei to license its patents for the first time in historic turnaround
items.description: Huawei and Qualcomm sign a multi-year patent cross-license covering 5G and AI, with Qualcomm buying some Huawei US patents.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Qualcomm will pay Huawei for patent rights under a multi-year cross-licensing agreement that highlights both 5G and AI technologies, and will buy some of Huawei’s U.S. patents outright, the firm announced. The joint announcement comes 25 years after Huawei began to pay Qualcomm for patents, a reversal that reportedly has Qualcomm paying for the first time. The agreement also covers compute and networking patents, and the patent purchase will close once it receives regulatory approval.The two companies’ licensing ties date back to 2001, when Huawei, then a Chinese telecom-infrastructure supplier, took a royalty-bearing license to build CDMA network equipment. Qualcomm, which once supplied chips for some Huawei phones, stopped counting royalties from Huawei in its revenue in early 2025.The “broad patent license agreement” allows “cross licenses” and reflects both companies’ commitment to intellectual property rights and to licensing consistent with “fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory (FRAND) principles.” The deal involves no other business cooperation, Huawei said, according to SCMP; this implies no chip sales are involved. The deal follows a settled back royalty dispute in 2020, the U.S. revoking Qualcomm’s license to sell some hardware to Huawei in 2024, and the expiration of Huawei’s license by early 2025.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Qualcomm’s patent purchase covers compute, AI, networking, and “other technologies,” according to the announcement, but the number of patents was not disclosed, nor was any value figure. Each company credits the other’s portfolio. This suggests that the two are trading official recognition of each other’s patents.Huawei says that, with the Qualcomm deal, the total value of its patent-licensing contracts will top $6.9 billion, counting from its first licensing income from Motorola in 2011. Since 2021, it says, its licensing business has brought in more than the company pays for other firms’ patents. In August, the company signed a multi-year Wi-Fi patent cross-license with HP and, as of 2025, the company held 165,000 active granted patents worldwide. You may like US allows Chinese telecom giant ZTE to purchase Nvidia H200 AI chips Huawei details AI accelerator roadmap, pulls in next-generation Ascend NPUs by several quarters First Nvidia H200 shipments reach China, ByteDance and Tencent take deliveries as Beijing loosens its import block Huawei has also gone to court to enforce its patents, as in a 2024 lawsuit against MediaTek. It halted royalty payments to Qualcomm in 2018, and its general counsel testified for the FTC about Qualcomm’s licensing terms in the agency’s 2019 antitrust trial against the chipmaker. Huawei can now take some satisfaction in leveling the playing field with Qualcomm.No timetable has been given for closing the patent purchase. Qualcomm’s Q4 report is expected next month, but its fiscal year ended before the announcement, so the deal will not make it into those numbers. The company also renewed its Apple license last month, effective April 1, 2027, after the current extension ends. items.titleZh: 高通将向华为支付专利许可费，历史性逆转首次出现
items.descriptionZh:
高通与华为宣布达成一项多年专利交叉许可协议，高通向华为支付专利权利金，并将直接购买华为部分美国专利。协议突出5G和AI技术，同时还覆盖计算和网络专利。华为表示，该交易不涉及其他业务合作，据南华早报报道，这意味着不涉及芯片销售。专利购买将在获得监管批准后完成，但双方未披露涉及专利数量和交易金额。此次联合声明距华为开始向高通支付专利费约25年，形成明显角色反转：据报道，高通首次成为向华为付费的一方。

从背景看，两家公司的许可关系可追溯至2001年。当时华为还是中国电信基础设施供应商，为制造CDMA网络设备而向高通取得付费专利许可。高通也曾为部分华为手机供应芯片，但从2025年初起，高通不再将来自华为的版税计入营收。此前，双方在2020年解决了一项回授权纠纷；2024年，美国撤销了高通向华为出售部分硬件的许可；到2025年初，华为原有许可到期。此次新协议正是在这些节点之后达成。双方称，这项“广泛专利许可协议”允许交叉许可，体现了两家公司对知识产权以及按照“公平、合理、非歧视（FRAND）原则”进行许可的承诺。

从技术原理看，这类交叉许可的核心是：双方在5G、AI、计算和网络等领域互相授权使用对方的专利技术，从而降低标准必要专利实施中的诉讼风险和许可摩擦。FRAND原则是通信标准专利许可中的关键机制，要求标准必要专利持有人以公平、合理、非歧视的条件授权。高通还将直接购买华为部分美国专利，涉及计算、AI、网络及其他技术，这意味着相关专利所有权将发生转让，而不只是许可使用。其创新性和象征意义在于，华为从历史上的主要被许可方，进一步成为向高通收取专利费并出售专利资产的一方，说明其在5G、AI及相关计算和网络领域的专利组合价值获得认可。需要指出的是，这里的AI技术是专利层面的覆盖，并非具体AI芯片架构、算力、制程或产品合作。

在可比较的数据方面，原文没有披露专利数量、交易金额、支付费率，也没有任何芯片性能、功耗、算力等参数，因此不存在可直接对比的AI芯片性能指标。但可量化的信息包括：双方许可关系始于2001年；华为自2011年从摩托罗拉获得首次许可收入以来，其专利许可合同总价值在本次与高通交易后将超过69亿美元；自2021年以来，华为许可业务收入已超过其向其他公司支付的专利费；截至2025年，华为在全球持有16.5万件有效授权专利。2025年8月，华为还与惠普签署了多年Wi-Fi专利交叉许可。华为也曾通过法院执行专利，例如2024年起诉联发科。华为在2018年停止向高通支付版税，其总法律顾问还在美国联邦贸易委员会2019年针对高通的 antitrust 审判中就高通的许可条款作证。此次协议没有给出专利购买完成的时间表。高通第四财季报告预计下月发布，但其财年在公告前已经结束，因此该交易不会计入这些业绩数字。高通还在上月续签了苹果许可，将在当前延长期结束后于2027年4月1日生效。

从影响和应用场景看，该协议覆盖5G、AI、计算和网络技术，可能影响基站、智能手机、AI计算平台和网络基础设施等领域的专利许可环境。它有助于减少双方在这些领域的专利诉讼摩擦，并推动更多交叉许可和FRAND实践。对华为而言，这意味着专利许可收入和专利地位进一步增强；对高通而言，它获得了华为相关专利授权和部分美国专利资产，但也要承担向华为付费的成本。不过，由于交易明确不涉及其他业务合作，也不涉及芯片销售，因此它不会直接改变高通对华为的芯片供应，也不代表双方在AI芯片产品、AI加速器或算力竞争上的合作。总体上，这一协议更像是一个知识产权格局变化的信号：在5G和AI相关专利领域，华为已从主要支付方转变为高通也需要付费的专利持有方。

items.title: OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design
items.description: OpenAI and Synopsys are developing GPT-Synopsys, a specialized semiconductor-design model that will directly operate Synopsys EDA tools
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter OpenAI and Synopsys have signed a multi-year agreement to jointly develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model optimized for semiconductor design using Synopsys's electronic design automation (EDA) tools. According to the September 30 announcement, the partnership “brings together OpenAI's advanced AI capabilities with Synopsys's industry-leading EDA tools and agentic AI capabilities to revolutionize the design of semiconductors.”Engineers would delegate to agents that run the tools and execute the required processes until the work is ready for review. The companies say this would allow design teams to evaluate more options and deliver more sophisticated chips. Under the preferred partner agreement, OpenAI is licensing Synopsys's tools to develop the model — which will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure — after which the companies will jointly release the product and share revenue. The announcement did not disclose a release date or a pricing structure.AI in chip design so farEngineers use EDA tools to design and verify chips before manufacturing. This multi-step process begins with writing the hardware description in register-transfer level (RTL) code and using synthesis software to convert it into logic gates. Next, physical design tools lay out the circuit elements and route the connections between them. Lastly, designers close timing, verify functionality, and ensure manufacturing compliance before tapeout for fabrication.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Each of these stages requires several iterations — repeatedly running various tools and troubleshooting issues — to balance critical trade-offs: power, performance, and silicon area (PPA). Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens EDA have dominated this market for these tools long before the current AI boom. Given the technology's capabilities, it is only natural that AI has found its way into the chip design process, creating a sort of “silicon designing silicon” loop.In March 2020, Synopsys launched DSO.ai (Design Space Optimization AI), a reinforcement learning tool that explores and learns from previous design optimizations to improve PPA. The company then launched Synopsys.ai Copilot in November 2023 — its first integration of generative AI — through a collaboration with Microsoft, integrating the Azure OpenAI service to provide natural language assistance within its engineering tools. You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond Synopsys debuts Autopilot platform for developing chips autonomously using AI The company’s current direction is Agentic AI, first revealed at the Design Automation Conference in July, where it showed an autonomous verification workflow built on Nvidia's Agent Toolkit and Nemotron 3 Ultra model. On September 28, two days before the OpenAI deal, Synopsys announced its Autopilot platform and AgentEngineer, a portfolio of seven long-horizon agents covering verification, implementation, analog, manufacturing, meshing, combustion, and EMC analysis. The company reported more than 50 engagements, with availability planned for late 2026.As detailed in our State of agentic AI in chip design tools roadmap, the move to agentic AI is not exclusive to Synopsys; Cadence and Siemens are also pitching autonomous design agents. Meanwhile, OpenAI, in collaboration with Broadcom, unveiled Jalapeño in June, the company’s first custom inference accelerator. OpenAI said the accelerator's design and optimization process leaned heavily on its AI models, allowing it to go from initial design to tape-out in just nine months. Now, GPT-Synopsys turns that internal experiment into a product.GPT-SynopsysAccording to the announcement, GPT-Synopsys will combine OpenAI's frontier models with Synopsys’s EDA software and domain expertise, allowing the model to reason about chip design and verification and operate Synopsys tools directly. Engineers would hand the model objectives such as PPA optimization, timing, and verification closure, while the agents run the tools, interpret the results, implement changes, and iterate toward verified outcomes for an engineer to review.In other words, the model would be capable of making engineering judgments involved in using Synopsys software. The companies describe it as learning to operate the tools like an expert engineer, interpreting their outputs and using the results to guide further changes. This is the proposed specialization that takes the model beyond connecting a general-purpose model to a set of tools.Synopsys’s EDA engines would perform the calculations and checks, with the model interpreting results and the agent software managing execution. GPT-Synopsys will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and is intended to integrate with Synopsys.ai and Autopilot, as well as work with customers’ own agent harnesses. Autopilot already provides services such as memory and governance. What to read next Amazon and Synopsys ink multi-year billion-dollar deal in multi-year IP agreement to accelerate AI chip design efforts ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs Synopsys says early technology engagements are underway with leading semiconductor customers, but didn't name any. The immediate audience is professional semiconductor-design teams, with companies developing their own custom silicon also likely to use it. Although the announcement covers semiconductor design generally, OpenAI has a particular interest in improving the hardware that runs its models. “By helping them build better chips, we can build better AI and bring it to more people,” said Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder. Whether the service also makes advanced design more accessible to smaller teams will depend on pricing and the expertise still required to supervise it.Questions and concernsThe recent announcement leaves a couple of questions and concerns unaddressed. First, hosting the model on OpenAI infrastructure raises concerns about how confidential designs are handled. The companies say customer data will be excluded from model training, encrypted at rest and in transit, and governed by configurable retention, audit, and permission controls. However, the release does not identify hosting regions or default retention periods. It also provides no contractual terms for ownership of generated outputs, use of third-party licensed design IP, or indemnities. The service's terms will likely address these questions.Another question is the practical economics for users. The industry has realized that handing over everything to AI doesn't always result in cost savings, at least for now. Sometimes the reverse is the case. Earlier this year, Uber’s CTO and an Nvidia executive said AI was more expensive than human workers, although many companies are reportedly fine with the extra cost. For GPT-Synopsys, advanced engineering reasoning and faster design-to-tapeout could justify the service, but model calls, EDA runs, integration, and human review all consume resources. The announcement did not include a pricing structure. It also didn't specify a launch date.Meanwhile, Synopsys’s main rival Cadence launched its ChipStack AI Super Agent in February for front-end design and verification, built on frontier LLMs. In April, the company announced a collaboration with Google to optimize ChipStack with Gemini on Google Cloud. At Computex, it extended ChipStack to what it calls Level-5 autonomy, powered by Nvidia's Nemotron models, with early access expected in the second half of 2026. The main difference is that while ChipStack is Cadence’s own agent software running on other companies’ general-purpose models, GPT-Synopsys will be an OpenAI model specifically trained to operate Synopsys’s tools.

items.titleZh: OpenAI与新思科技合作打造“GPT-Synopsys”以实现自主芯片设计
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI与Synopsys于9月30日宣布签署多年协议，将联合开发GPT-Synopsys。这是一个面向半导体设计的专用模型，基于Synopsys的电子设计自动化（EDA）工具优化。双方称，该合作把OpenAI的先进AI能力与Synopsys行业领先的EDA工具及智能体AI能力结合，目标是革新芯片设计。按照“优先合作伙伴协议”，OpenAI获授权使用Synopsys工具来开发模型，模型将运行在OpenAI托管的基础设施上；之后双方将联合发布产品并分享收入。公告未披露发布日期和定价结构。

背景方面，工程师使用EDA工具在制造前设计和验证芯片。流程从编写寄存器传输级（RTL）硬件描述开始，用综合软件转换为逻辑门；随后物理设计工具布局电路元件并布线；最后设计人员完成时序收敛、功能验证和制造合规检查，再送交流片。每个阶段都需要多轮迭代，反复运行各类工具并排查问题，以平衡功耗、性能和硅面积（PPA）等关键取舍。Synopsys、Cadence和Siemens EDA在AI热潮之前就长期主导这一市场。AI进入芯片设计后，形成了某种“硅设计硅”的循环。Synopsys早在2020年3月推出DSO.ai，用强化学习探索并学习既往设计优化，以改善PPA；2023年11月又与微软合作推出Synopsys.ai Copilot，首次集成生成式AI，通过Azure OpenAI服务在工程工具内提供自然语言辅助。其当前方向是智能体AI：7月在Design Automation Conference上展示了基于Nvidia Agent Toolkit和Nemotron 3 Ultra模型的自主验证工作流；9月28日，即OpenAI交易前两天，Synopsys发布Autopilot平台和AgentEngineer，包含七个长周期智能体，覆盖验证、实现、模拟、制造、网格划分、燃烧和EMC分析，已报告超过50个合作项目，计划2026年底可用。Cadence和Siemens也在推出自主设计智能体。OpenAI则与Broadcom合作，在6月发布Jalapeño，这是其首个定制推理加速器；OpenAI称该加速器的设计和优化过程大量依赖其AI模型，从初始设计到流片仅用9个月。GPT-Synopsys则是把这一内部实验转化为产品。

技术原理上，GPT-Synopsys将OpenAI的前沿模型与Synopsys的EDA软件及领域专业知识结合，使模型能够推理芯片设计与验证，并直接操作Synopsys工具。工程师可向模型提交PPA优化、时序收敛、验证收敛等目标，由智能体运行工具、解读结果、实施修改并迭代，直到形成可供工程师审核的已验证结果。换言之，模型要像专家工程师一样操作工具、理解输出，并据此指导后续修改，而不仅是把通用模型连接到一组工具上。Synopsys的EDA引擎负责计算和检查，模型解读结果，智能体软件管理执行。GPT-Synopsys将运行在OpenAI托管的基础设施上，计划集成到Synopsys.ai和Autopilot，也可与客户自有的智能体框架配合。Autopilot已提供记忆和治理等服务。Synopsys称已与领先半导体客户开展早期技术合作，但未点名。其直接受众是专业半导体设计团队，开发自研芯片的公司也可能使用。OpenAI尤其关注改进运行其模型的硬件。OpenAI总裁兼联合创始人Greg Brockman表示：“通过帮助他们造更好的芯片，我们可以造更好的AI，并把它带给更多人。”该服务是否能让小团队也更容易使用先进设计，将取决于定价以及仍需人类监督的专业能力。

问题和担忧方面，首先，将模型托管在OpenAI基础设施上，引发机密设计如何处理的担忧。双方称客户数据将被排除在模型训练之外，静态和传输中加密，并受可配置的保留、审计和权限控制约束；但发布信息未说明托管区域或默认保留期，也没有关于生成输出所有权、第三方授权设计IP使用或赔偿的合同条款。服务条款可能会回应这些问题。其次是用户的实际经济性。业界已意识到，把所有事情交给AI并不总能节省成本，至少目前如此，有时反而更贵。今年早些时候，Uber首席技术官和一位Nvidia高管称AI比人类员工更贵，尽管据报道许多公司接受这种额外成本。对GPT-Synopsys而言，高级工程推理和更快设计到流片可能证明其价值，但模型调用、EDA运行、集成和人工审核都会消耗资源。公告未包含定价结构，也未指定上市日期。竞争方面，Synopsys主要对手Cadence在2月推出ChipStack AI Super Agent，用于前端设计与验证，基于前沿LLM；4月宣布与Google合作，在Google Cloud上用Gemini优化ChipStack；在Computex上将其扩展到所谓Level-5自主性，由Nvidia Nemotron模型驱动，预计2026年下半年早期访问。关键区别在于：ChipStack是Cadence自己的智能体软件，运行在其他公司的通用模型上；GPT-Synopsys则是OpenAI专门训练来操作Synopsys工具的模型。

items.title: Elon Musk pledges SpaceXSI rebrand after Trump's executive order to use 'Super Intelligence' moniker
items.description: Elon Musk says he plans to rename SpaceXAI as SpaceXSI to reflect the new "Super Intelligence" moniker adopted in President Trump's executive order
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk has confirmed that SpaceXAI will change its name to SpaceXSI, to reflect the new moniker “Super Intelligence” coined by President Trump as a replacement for “Artificial Intelligence.” In an X post on September 4, Musk wrote, “Yes, we will make that change,” in response to an X user’s question about renaming the AI company. Musk had earlier posted, “No more AI. SI. It’s better,” following up the post with a photo of the cover page of Nick Bostrom's book, “Superintelligence.”President Donald Trump signed the executive order to officially rebrand “Artificial Intelligence” to “Super Intelligence” on September 29, 2026, during a high-level technology summit at the White House dubbed “Super Intelligence Luncheon.” The administration argued that “artificial” implies something fake and that “super intelligence” better captures the technology's true scale and potential. Several Federal agencies have already implemented the rebrand.Six days after the summit, President Trump formally launched the “Super Intelligence Force” (SIF) through a presidential mandate and public announcement via Truth Social on Sunday, October 4, following up on his earlier promise to launch a force that will “cherish” the technology and “help it grow.” The Force will report directly to the White House and will oversee domestic AI policy, ensure American AI dominance over global rivals like China, and interface directly with the private tech sector.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Regarding the rebrand, it is unclear how the numerous American AI companies with “AI” in their names and products intend to proceed. Furthermore, the total number of registered .ai domains has officially surpassed 1 million globally. Registrations had reportedly generated an estimated $96.4 million for the 2026 budget of Antigua — a tiny Caribbean island nation with “.ai” as its country-code top-level domain — accounting for nearly half of total government revenue.Following the announcement, speculators are frantically buying up .si domains, often registering look-alike domains mirroring existing .ai sites. Musk has yet to implement the “SI” nomenclature across his companies, with the X.ai domain still featuring “AI” and “Artificial Intelligence” in all copies sitewide, as of this report. items.titleZh: Elon Musk pledges SpaceXSI rebrand after Trump's executive order to use 'Super Intelligence' moniker
items.descriptionZh:
据 Tom's Hardware 报道，埃隆·马斯克已确认 SpaceXAI 将更名为 SpaceXSI，以配合美国总统特朗普提出的新术语“Super Intelligence”（超级智能），用来取代“Artificial Intelligence”（人工智能）。9月4日，马斯克在 X 上回应网友关于更名的提问时写道“是的，我们会改”，并在此前发帖称“不要再叫 AI 了，叫 SI，更好”，还附上尼克·博斯特罗姆《超级智能》一书封面。

背景上，特朗普于2026年9月29日在白宫一场名为“Super Intelligence Luncheon”的高级别科技峰会上签署行政命令，正式将“Artificial Intelligence”重新命名为“Super Intelligence”。其政府认为“artificial”暗示虚假，而“super intelligence”更能体现这项技术的真实规模和潜力。多个联邦机构已开始执行这一更名。

六天后，即10月4日星期日，特朗普通过总统授权和 Truth Social 公开宣布正式启动“Super Intelligence Force”（SIF，超级智能部队/力量）。该机构直接向白宫汇报，负责监督美国国内AI政策，确保美国在全球AI竞争中相对于中国等对手的主导地位，并直接与私营科技部门对接。此前他曾承诺建立一支“珍视”该技术并“帮助其成长”的力量。

报道指出，围绕更名仍存在不确定性：大量名称或产品中含有“AI”的美国AI公司打算如何应对尚不清楚。同时，全球注册的 .ai 域名总数已正式超过100万个；这些注册为加勒比小岛国安提瓜2026年预算带来约9640万美元收入，占其政府总收入近一半，因为 .ai 是安提瓜的国家代码顶级域名。更名消息宣布后，投机者疯狂抢购 .si 域名，常注册与现有 .ai 网站相似的仿冒域名。马斯克尚未在其公司全面实施“SI”命名：截至报道时，X.ai 域名及全站文案仍使用“AI”和“Artificial Intelligence”。

核心上，此事并非新的AI技术性能发布，也没有芯片、模型参数或基准数据披露。其“创新”主要在于术语、品牌和政策框架重构：用“超级智能”替代“人工智能”，并设立白宫直属的 SIF 来统筹国内AI政策、国际竞争和私营部门协调。影响可能波及企业品牌与域名策略、政府文件用语、AI产业监管，以及 .ai/.si 域名生态；但实际执行、企业跟进程度和技术含义仍有待观察。

items.content: Google may be expanding its “Call for Me” AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a “Gemini Calling” introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include “Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late” and “Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner.”Based on those examples, even with this expansion, Gemini would likely be limited to basic, text message-like calls. While Google’s AI might not automate an entire catch-up phone call with your relatives, it could deliver quick messages to people who prefer a phone call, miss texts often, or even still have a landline phone.Android Authority also says it found “granular permissions” for Gemini actions in individual apps, including what appear to be settings for phone call permissions. These settings would allow users to pick and choose which app capabilities they want to allow Gemini to access, potentially giving users an option to opt out of receiving incoming automated calls from Gemini. However, as Android Authority notes, it’s also possible Google might not publicly release this expansion or the granular Gemini app settings.

items.titleZh: Gemini为我通话可能会告诉你妈妈你要迟到了
items.descriptionZh:
根据 Android Authority 的 APK 拆解，Google 可能正在把其“Call for Me”AI 功能从商务通话扩展到个人通讯，让用户通过 Gemini 向朋友和家人发送电话消息。拆解中出现了名为“Gemini Calling”的介绍页面，示例指令包括“打电话给妈妈，告诉她我会迟到 15 分钟”和“打电话给 John，问他是否来吃晚饭”。这表明 Gemini 可能获得发起电话呼叫并传递简短信息的能力。

背景上，Call for Me 原本更多与商务或事务性通话相关，而新线索显示 Google 想把它用于亲友之间的短信式沟通。所谓 APK 拆解，是指从 Android 应用安装包中提前发现尚未正式发布的功能，因此目前不能确认该功能一定会上线。

技术原理上，这类功能通常由 Gemini 解析用户的自然语言指令，提取联系人、通话目的和要传达的内容，再通过电话网络自动拨号，并以合成语音或类似交互式语音的方式把信息告诉对方。创新点不只是“AI 打电话”，还包括将复杂的语音助手能力压缩到简单、可靠、可重复的短消息场景。根据示例，它很可能不会自动完成一次完整的叙旧电话，而是像“语音短信”一样传递具体信息。

报道还提到，拆解中发现了 Gemini 在单个应用中的“细粒度权限”设置，包括电话通话权限。这意味着用户可能可以逐项选择允许 Gemini 访问哪些应用能力，甚至可以选择不接收 Gemini 自动打来的电话。这有助于缓解隐私、骚扰和自动化通话方面的担忧。

性能参数方面，目前没有延迟、通话成功率、支持机型、语言范围或正式发布时间等数据。与现有商务通话场景相比，这次扩展的主要变化是从商业用途走向个人通讯，但能力边界仍可能局限于基础消息传递。其潜在应用包括：给更爱接电话、经常漏看短信、甚至仍在使用座机的人快速传话，例如通知迟到、确认晚餐、提醒事项等。

不过，Android Authority 也指出，Google 可能不会公开发布这一扩展或细粒度权限设置。因此，目前这仍属于 APK 线索层面的可能性，而非正式产品发布。若最终落地，它可能让 Gemini 成为电话与短信之间的 AI 中介，但也会引发对自动来电、隐私授权和真实通话体验的讨论。

history.title: Gigaphoton debuts neon recycling system with claimed 50% recovery rate
history.description: New neon gas recycling systems promise to reduce the demand for the noble gas at major chip manufacturers using DUV lithography. But as that technology is supplanted, this much-needed fix may only be needed temporarily.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Japanese semiconductor lithography tool maker Gigaphoton has developed a novel neon gas recycling system named hTGM for its argon fluoride (ArF) excimer lasers. The method has demonstrated a 50% recycling rate, with hopes that it can be improved dramatically with adjusted configurations, Business Wire reports. This could help fill a gap in the chip supply chain caused by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Before 2022, Ukraine shipped up to 50% of the neon gas used in the semiconductor industry, but its major producers had to stop exports, raising concerns over chip supply. 70% of global neon production is used in semiconductor manufacturing, particularly in advanced DUV processes.In the aftermath, China, Taiwan, and South Korea all increased their own domestic Neon production efforts, but various chip manufacturers also integrated recycling systems at various points during the fabrication process. Gigaphoton's more efficient ArF lasers with neon recycling could further help close those loops, reducing material costs and further reducing reliance on global supply chains.It's not the only company pushing this technology forward, either. At the start of September, Japanese environmental protection company Kanken Techno demonstrated its own Neon gas recycling system for excimer lasers at SemiCon Taiwan. It demonstrated a recycling rate of over 90%, suggesting there is considerable headroom to improve this process in the future.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: What makes Neon so scarce?Neon is one of a handful of noble gases, making it inert under standard conditions and easy to handle. However, the ease with which it vaporizes and its limited bonding ability mean it is relatively scarce in Earth's atmosphere, making it scarce. It is most efficiently obtained through fractional distillation of super-cooled air, making it most affordable to obtain as a byproduct of other processes. For decades, Ukrainian steel-mill air-separation units produced crude neon from large-scale air-separation units (ASUs), and then refined it in-country via a pair of key companies.That meant that when Russia escalated its war against Ukraine into a full-scale invasion in 2022 and Ukrainian neon refiners shut down production, there was an immediate global response. You may like Lumentum CEO warns of impending bottleneck on critical material used for silicon photonics China's DUV technology 'at a similar stage to ASML in 2004,' analyst claims ASML says it sold 'absolutely nothing' in Europe in 2026 As SFA Oxford explains, South Korea accelerated domestic production and implemented a large-scale, national neon recycling initiative focused on in-fab recovery. Taiwan installed purification systems in existing blast-furnace ASUs, developing its own domestic supply chain. By utilizing its national infrastructure, it targeted complete self-sufficiency in neon gas production within a few years.China integrated neon gas purification into many elements of its industrial base, twinning it with steel and petrochemical production facilities. The U.S. also responded with the development of new ASUs at Gulf-coast petrochemical hubs, but those aren't expected to meaningfully improve American neon supplies until near the end of the decade.Lithography accounts for around 70% of global neon use, particularly in more advanced DUV processes — though crucially, not in EUV lithography, which uses a tin-plasma laser instead. With global DUV-produced semiconductor supply rapidly advancing in the wake of the AI buildout, neon supply is an important component in the chip supply chain, which has rapidly evolved to become a key asset within strategic defence and global trade.Working with what you've gotFor individual companies that can't directly control their supply chains, recycling has been a much more immediate focus. The first neon gas recycling systems were qualified for use with Cymer excimer ArF lasers at the end of 2023, and Samsung and SK Hynix became the first of the major memory makers to implement neon gas recycling in 2024.Gigaphoton previously offered neon recycling with KrF (krypton fluoride) lasers, but has now extended that recycling capability to ArF lasers as well. It claims a single hTGM for ArF unit can reduce neon gas consumption by up to 470 kilotres per year, representing substantial material cost savings, as well as reducing company reliance on a global supply chain that has been sufficiently unstable in recent years. What to read next Analyst firm says ASML unlikely to back particle accelerator chipmaking tech Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined — Beijing's nascent lithography tools target DUV production at five machines a year, and an EUV prototype with no chips China stockpiled 343 immersion DUV tools for advanced chipmaking However, its claims of a 50% recycling rate aren't exactly groundbreaking. Cymer's excimer laser neon recovery system demonstrated that same level of efficiency in 2015, and Gigaphoton's own testing suggested a potential peak for ArF recovery of over 90% in 2017.That suggests it should be able to ramp up its efforts to a higher percentage quite swiftly. Especially since fellow Japanese firm Kanken Techno recently unveiled a neon recycling system with over 90% efficiency. Kanken works with both major ArF laser developers and is currently going through the certification process, with expected approval in the near future.A temporary fix?With neon gas recycling during chip production effectively solved, it may be that the supply of neon for the chip industry has proved to be a temporary problem. But it may be a temporary solution too, as the use of neon within the industry may be set to shrink dramatically in the years to come.EUV lithography can build far more complex chips than DUV, and offers a future path beyond the need for neon gas usage in excimer lasers as newer electronics adopt the more capable chip designs. On top of that, alternative technologies to DUV are being developed which could produce the same DUV light to generate advanced semiconductors, but without the need for noble or toxic gases.Solid-state laser technologies have been rapidly developing in recent years, though last year's Chinese efforts are still below required industrial power thresholds. Nanoimprint lithography also holds promise as a DUV alternative, as well as cutting costs by a comparative 90%.There are still huge hurdles in performance and certification, as well as integration with existing fabrication plans and supply chains. But the potential to move beyond the need for neon gas within semiconductor lithography is there. Over the coming years, the combination of laser neon recycling systems and alternative manufacturing techniques could reduce the need for international neon sources to a fraction of existing levels.

history.titleZh: Gigaphoton推出氖气回收系统，声称回收率达50%
history.descriptionZh:
日本半导体光刻工具制造商 Gigaphoton 开发出名为 hTGM 的新型氖气回收系统，用于氩氟（ArF）准分子激光器。该系统已实现 50% 的氖气回收率，公司希望调整配置后大幅提升。Business Wire 报道称，这有助于填补俄乌战争造成的芯片供应链缺口。2022 年前，乌克兰供应半导体行业最多 50% 的氖气，但其主要生产商停止出口，引发芯片供应担忧。全球约 70% 的氖气产量用于半导体制造，尤其先进 DUV 工艺。此后，中国大陆、中国台湾地区和韩国均加大本土氖气生产，芯片制造商也在制造环节整合回收系统。Gigaphoton 为 ArF 激光加入氖回收，可进一步形成闭环，降低材料成本和对全球供应链的依赖。与此同时，日本环保企业 Kanken Techno 也在 9 月初 SEMICON Taiwan 展示了用于准分子激光的氖回收系统，回收率超过 90%，显示该工艺仍有很大提升空间。

氖是惰性气体，标准条件下不易反应、易于处理，但容易挥发且键合能力有限，在地球大气中相对稀缺。最有效的获取方式是对超冷空气进行分馏，而作为其他工业过程的副产品获取最为经济。几十年来，乌克兰钢厂的大型空气分离装置（ASU）生产粗氖，再由两家关键公司在本国精炼。2022 年俄乌冲突全面升级后，乌克兰氖精炼商停产，全球随即作出反应。韩国加速国内生产，并实施大规模国家氖回收倡议，重点放在晶圆厂内回收；中国台湾地区在现有高炉 ASU 中安装净化系统，发展本土供应链，目标是在几年内实现氖气完全自给；中国大陆将氖气净化整合进钢铁、石化等工业基础；美国则在墨西哥湾沿岸石化中心开发新 ASU，但预计到本十年末才能明显改善美国氖供应。光刻是氖的主要用途之一，尤其在先进 DUV 工艺中，但 EUV 不使用氖，而是使用锡等离子激光。随着 AI 建设推动 DUV 半导体供应，氖供应已成为芯片供应链以及战略防务和全球贸易中的关键资产。

对无法直接控制供应链的企业而言，回收是更直接的应对方式。首批氖回收系统于 2023 年底获准用于 Cymer 准分子 ArF 激光器，三星和 SK 海力士则在 2024 年成为首批实施氖回收的主要存储制造商。Gigaphoton 此前已为 KrF 激光提供氖回收，如今将能力扩展到 ArF。公司声称，单个用于 ArF 的 hTGM 单元每年最多可减少 470 千单位（原文写作 kilotres）的氖气消耗，带来可观的物料成本节省，并降低对近年不稳定全球供应链的依赖。不过，50% 的回收率并非突破性水平：Cymer 的准分子激光氖回收系统在 2015 年就展示过同等效率，Gigaphoton 自己在 2017 年的测试也显示 ArF 回收潜在峰值可超过 90%。这意味着其回收率应能较快提升，尤其 Kanken Techno 最近已推出效率超过 90% 的氖回收系统。Kanken 与主要 ArF 激光开发商合作，目前正进行认证，预计不久后获批。

从未来看，芯片生产中的氖回收已有效解决，氖供应可能只是暂时问题，但回收也可能只是临时方案，因为氖在半导体行业中的使用量可能大幅缩小。EUV 能制造比 DUV 更复杂的芯片，随着新电子设备采用更先进设计，未来路径可能超越准分子激光对氖的需求。此外，替代 DUV 的技术正在开发，可产生相同 DUV 光来制造先进半导体，却无需稀有或有毒气体。固态激光技术近年发展迅速，但中国去年的相关努力仍低于工业功率阈值；纳米压印光刻也有望替代 DUV，并相对降低约 90% 成本。这些方案在性能、认证以及与现有晶圆厂和供应链整合方面仍有巨大障碍，但摆脱半导体光刻对氖气依赖的潜力已经存在。未来，激光氖回收系统与替代制造技术结合，可能将国际氖源需求降至现有水平的一小部分。

history.title: Why Telecom Operators Are Building Their AI Strategy on Open Models
history.description: Telecom operators are increasingly building their AI strategies on open models — and the reasons go beyond mere cost.  Open models give telcos the ability to trust, control and customize AI across their most critical workloads — from autonomous networks to customer care.  NVIDIA’s latest State of AI in Telecommunications report reflects this shift, with […]
history.content: Telecom operators are increasingly building their AI strategies on open models — and the reasons go beyond mere cost. Open models give telcos the ability to trust, control and customize AI across their most critical workloads — from autonomous networks to customer care. NVIDIA’s latest State of AI in Telecommunications report reflects this shift, with 89% of respondents reporting that open source models and software are important to their company’s AI strategy. For operators, the strategic value of open models is fivefold: They expand access to frontier‑level intelligence at lower cost, allowing operators to reserve closed models for the workloads where they drive the most value. Independent benchmarks such as the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 show that leading open models are becoming more competitive across demanding reasoning, coding, scientific and agentic workloads. They support telco‑specific customization, with open weights and training recipes that operators can fine‑tune for their own operations using network, customer and industry data. They enable trustworthy AI by giving telcos greater visibility into and control over model artifacts and behavior, so models can be evaluated, adapted and governed in alignment with regulations and business policies. They enable flexible, secure deployment: teams can size and optimize open models to run across public clouds, private infrastructure and edge environments. They unlock the opportunity for telcos to deliver locally adapted AI services to enterprise and government customers by hosting and fine-tuning open models. Open Foundations, Tuned for Telecom Operations The NVIDIA Nemotron family of open models provides frontier-level reasoning performance optimized for agentic workflows, as well as speech capabilities for voice applications, with open weights, training data and recipes. SoftBank Corp. illustrates how an operator can use open models as a basis for developing and continuously advancing its telecom-specific AI capabilities. “Open models allow SoftBank Corp. to build on the rapid progress of global foundation models while applying the network knowledge and operational expertise we have accumulated over many years,” said Rajeev Koodli, principal fellow of SoftBank Corp. and senior vice president of SB Telecom America. “We are using open foundations extensively, including NVIDIA Nemotron models and others, in developing our SoftBank Large Telecom Model, continuously advancing it for telecom-specific use cases such as network operations, design and overall management.” In addition, NVIDIA is collaborating with partners to help turn open models into practical building blocks for telecom AI. NVIDIA announced the 30-billion-parameter Nemotron 3 Large Telco Model (LTM), fine-tuned by AdaptKey on open source telecom datasets to deliver accuracy gains for telecom-specific tasks. This gives operators an open baseline that can understand telecom industry terminology and reason effectively through telecom operations workflows such as network configuration and customer incident triage. To help operators customize the Nemotron 3 LTM and other open models with their own operational data, NVIDIA released the full recipe that walks through the end-to-end fine-tuning pipeline for adapting open models to operator-specific networks, customers and procedures using NVIDIA NeMo open libraries. Scale Open Models Into Production Workflows Open models are a critical building block, but it takes more than models to bring autonomous telecom operations safely into production. For AT&T, the value of model choice lies in making that flexibility operational in alignment with its business priorities. “At AT&T, we believe the future of AI is not about choosing a single model; it’s about intelligently matching every workload to the right combination of performance, cost and control,” said Andy Markus, chief data and AI officer of AT&T. “Open models are essential to that approach, and with NVIDIA, we can bring that model-choice strategy into production with the scale, reliability and governance our business requires.” Operators need pipelines that prepare and protect their data for model fine‑tuning by anonymizing sensitive records and generating privacy‑preserving synthetic datasets. They also need a platform that can turn open models into governed, autonomous agentic workflows. NVIDIA provides that end-to-end platform, powered by NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, and spanning data pipelines, open models, agent orchestration, secure runtimes and simulation. Together with a strong partner ecosystem building at every layer of this platform, telecom operators have a clear path to translate the benefits of open models into production-ready AI workflows. Create a Platform for Local AI Innovation As telecom operators build AI infrastructure aligned with national AI strategies, open models are giving them a foundation to deliver AI services tailored to local languages, industries, regulations and data governance requirements. Operators across countries can fine-tune open models for local-language and industry-specific needs, as well as host open models on their trusted platforms that customers can consume directly or build on with their own data and applications. For Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, one of Indonesia’s largest telecom operators, that means building AI that reflects the country’s own language and culture through its Sahabat-AI family of open source models. “For countries like Indonesia, the value of open models goes beyond access to powerful AI. It is about adapting that intelligence to our own language, culture, data and real-world needs,” said Chirag Sukhadia, chief data and AI officer of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison. “Sahabat-AI puts this into practice, using open models as a foundation to build AI that understands Indonesia and can be developed for local applications. This allows us not only to adopt AI, but to build capabilities around it and enable more Indonesians to create with AI on their own terms.” Learn more about NVIDIA technologies for telecommunications.
history.author: Kanika Atri
history.titleZh: 为何电信运营商基于开放模型构建其AI战略
history.descriptionZh:
电信运营商正越来越多地基于开放模型制定AI战略，原因不只是成本。开放模型让运营商能够在其最关键的业务负载中信任、控制和定制AI，从自治网络到客户服务。NVIDIA最新的《电信行业AI现状》报告反映了这一转变：89%的受访者表示，开源模型和软件对其公司的AI战略很重要。对运营商而言，开放模型的战略价值体现在五个方面：以更低成本获得前沿级智能，从而把闭源模型留给价值最高的负载；支持电信专属定制，运营商可利用开放权重和训练配方，结合网络、客户和行业数据对模型进行微调；实现可信AI，让运营商更清楚地了解并控制模型工件和行为，从而按照监管要求和业务政策评估、调整和治理模型；支持灵活、安全的部署，团队可以调整和优化开放模型，使其运行在公有云、私有基础设施和边缘环境中；解锁新机会，运营商可通过托管和微调开放模型，向企业和政府客户提供本地适配的AI服务。

NVIDIA的Nemotron系列开放模型提供面向智能体工作流优化的前沿级推理性能，以及用于语音应用的语音能力，并开放权重、训练数据和配方。软银公司展示了运营商如何以开放模型为基础，开发和持续提升电信专属AI能力。软银公司首席研究员、SB Telecom America高级副总裁Rajeev Koodli表示，开放模型让软银能够在全球基础模型快速进步的基础上，应用其多年积累的网络知识和运营经验。软银正在广泛使用开放基础模型，包括NVIDIA Nemotron等，来开发其“软银大型电信模型”，并持续推进网络运营、设计和整体管理等电信专属用例。

此外，NVIDIA正与合作伙伴协作，将开放模型转化为电信AI的实用构建模块。NVIDIA发布了300亿参数的Nemotron 3 Large Telco Model（LTM），由AdaptKey基于开源电信数据集微调，可提升电信专属任务的准确性。这为运营商提供了一个开放基线，能够理解电信行业术语，并有效推理网络配置、客户事件分诊等电信运营工作流。为帮助运营商用自身运营数据定制Nemotron 3 LTM和其他开放模型，NVIDIA还发布了完整配方，介绍如何使用NVIDIA NeMo开放库，完成将开放模型适配到运营商特定网络、客户和流程的端到端微调流水线。

将开放模型扩展到生产工作流，仅靠模型还不够，还需要把自治电信运营安全地投入生产。对AT&T而言，模型选择的价值在于将这种灵活性与其业务优先级对齐并投入运营。AT&T首席数据与AI官Andy Markus表示，AI的未来不是选择单一模型，而是智能地将每个工作负载匹配到性能、成本和控制的正确组合；开放模型对这一方法至关重要，借助NVIDIA，AT&T可以按业务所需的规模、可靠性和治理，将模型选择战略投入生产。运营商需要流水线来准备和保护用于模型微调的数据，包括匿名化敏感记录和生成保护隐私的合成数据集；还需要一个平台，将开放模型转化为受治理的自治智能体工作流。NVIDIA提供由NVIDIA AI Enterprise软件和NVIDIA Agent Toolkit支持的端到端平台，覆盖数据流水线、开放模型、智能体编排、安全运行时和仿真。再加上在这一平台各层构建的强大合作伙伴生态，电信运营商已有清晰路径，将开放模型的优势转化为生产级AI工作流。

在电信运营商建设与国家AI战略一致的AI基础设施时，开放模型为其提供了基础，可提供适配本地语言、行业、监管和数据治理要求的AI服务。各国运营商可针对本地语言和行业需求微调开放模型，并在其可信平台上托管开放模型，供客户直接使用，或基于自身数据和应用进行构建。对印尼最大电信运营商之一Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison而言，这意味着通过其开源模型系列Sahabat-AI，构建体现印尼自身语言和文化的AI。Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison首席数据与AI官Chirag Sukhadia表示，对印尼这样的国家，开放模型的价值不只是获得强大AI，而是让智能适配本国语言、文化、数据和现实需求。Sahabat-AI将这一理念付诸实践，以开放模型为基础，构建理解印尼的AI，并可为本地应用开发。这不仅让印尼采用AI，也能围绕AI建设能力，让更多印尼人按自己的方式用AI创造。

history.title: EV charging company plans to deploy 100,000 Nvidia GPUs in pods at its roadside sites across the US
history.description: EV charging firm Xeal plans to use its existing U.S. network to deploy the 'world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity.'
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter EV charging firm Xeal plans to use its existing U.S. network to deploy the “world’s first edge inference compute network using idle EV charging capacity.” The big idea is that it already has 1,600+ locations and 200MW of permitted, installed electrical infrastructure, so it aims to “deploy over 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs” at these sites. Thus it has developed Latient Pods (pictured), with each containing up to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUs. We hope charging location security will be adequate to keep thieves away from these cabinets, as they are probably worth $2M+ each.Nikhil Bharadwaj, co-founder and CEO of Xeal, explained that Latient Pods can deliver inference compute today while new data centers are still being built. “Latient is the fastest way to bring new compute online, tapping already permitted and grid-connected, yet idle energy capacity, located right where it's needed for ultra-low latency, with no water hookup requirements,” highlighted the exec. Grid interconnect is said to be one of the trickiest things for those looking to bring new compute online, but Xeal’s EV charging sites, which “typically operate at less than 10% of permitted capacity,” can deliver processing power via a distributed network across a metropolitan area.An Nvidia rep also praised the upcoming Latient Pod network for being an innovative way to bring low-latency inference closer to users while making better use of infrastructure that has already been built.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: In the rendered image from Xeal, a Latient Pod looks quite a lot like a broadband fiber cabinet that you might have on your street. A pod will boast the following specs/features:Powered by idle EV charging capacityUp to 48 Nvidia Hopper or Blackwell Ultra GPUsSelf-contained independent cooling, no water hookup requiredQuiet operation at less than 65 dBs (comparable to a washing machine)Fixed rental or ancillary revenue for site ownerAdds up to $1 million in property value for little-to-no investmentAll power bills covered as a tenant pass-throughPotential savings for EV charging customersBuilt to withstand the outdoors, NEMA 4 enclosureInstalled and running in hoursIf Xeal has 1,600+ locations, and one Latient Pod has up to 48 GPUs, its touted purchasing target of 100,000 Nvidia GPUs suggests some sites will have more than a single pod at the location. Or perhaps it intends to build more EV sites, up to nearly 2,100 in total. You may like Elon Musk's SpaceXAI to add another 660,000 AI GPUs this year, nearing a total of 1.44 million in operation Startups want to rent your idle gaming PC for AI tasks Nvidia weighs $250 billion guarantee so OpenAI can lease SoftBank's 10-gigawatt Ohio campus, report claims It claims that the location of its pods around metro areas, a feature dubbed Metro Edge, offers sub-20ms latency, a significant speedup over inference located in a distant data center.We’ve previously reported on EVs and distributed computing, but in a slightly different context. Last year we discussed Elon Musk’s proposal to make use of the untapped asset of the millions of Tesla cars out there. He called it “100 gigawatts of inference” that could be used when the vehicles are “bored.”Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsMeanwhile, we must remember that EV charging stations are already being targeted by thieves. We reported about a ‘plague’ of electric car charger cable thefts driven simply by the copper scrap value of the hefty cables used at the sites. Imagine the security that would be required if/when Latient Pods are deployed, stuffed with extremely expensive GPUs. 48 Blackwell GPUs would be worth around $2,000,000 according to 2024 figures – so surely much more by now.The first Latient Pod will be online by the end of the year, says Xeal. history.titleZh: 电动汽车充电公司计划在全美路边站点部署10万块英伟达GPU算力舱
history.descriptionZh:
美国电动车充电企业Xeal宣布，计划利用其现有的美国充电网络，部署“全球首个使用闲置电动车充电容量的边缘推理计算网络”。Xeal目前拥有1600多个站点，以及200MW已获许可并完成安装的电力基础设施。公司希望在这些站点部署超过10万块NVIDIA GPU，从而把原本利用率不高的充电站电力容量转化为分布式AI推理算力。

为此，Xeal开发了Latient Pod。每个Latient Pod最多可容纳48块NVIDIA Hopper或Blackwell Ultra GPU。从外观上看，它类似街道上的宽带光纤机柜，但内部是高密度AI计算设备。其核心创新在于：不再等待新建大型数据中心和漫长的电网互联，而是直接利用已经并网、已获许可但通常闲置的EV充电站容量。Xeal表示，其充电站点通常只运行在许可容量的不到10%，因此有大量电力可供边缘计算使用。Latient Pod采用自包含独立冷却系统，无需接水，噪音低于65分贝，约等于洗衣机；具备NEMA 4户外防护能力，可在数小时内完成安装并运行。

在性能方面，Xeal将这种分布式布局称为“Metro Edge”，即把推理算力部署在都市区周边，从而提供低于20毫秒的延迟，相比把推理任务放在远端数据中心有显著加速。公司认为，Latient Pod是当前最快把新算力上线的方式之一，因为它利用的是已经许可、已经并网、但尚未充分利用的能源容量，并且位于需要超低延迟服务的地点附近，同时不需要水连接。英伟达方面也称赞该网络是一种创新方式，可以把低延迟推理更靠近用户，并更好利用已有基础设施。

从规模看，如果Xeal拥有1600多个站点，而每个Latient Pod最多支持48块GPU，那么其10万块NVIDIA GPU的采购目标意味着部分站点将部署多个Pod，或者Xeal可能将EV站点扩展到接近2100个。每个Pod的商业模式对站点所有者也有吸引力：可获得固定租金或附加收入，几乎无需投资即可为物业增加最高100万美元价值；电费以租户转嫁方式覆盖；还可能为EV充电客户带来潜在节省。

不过，安全是明显风险。电动车充电站已经频繁成为盗窃目标，尤其是粗大充电电缆因铜材回收价值而遭窃。Latient Pod内装满昂贵GPU，按2024年数据，48块Blackwell GPU价值约200万美元，如今只会更高。因此，部署这些机柜需要足够安保。Xeal表示，第一个Latient Pod将在今年年底前上线。此前也有类似分布式算力设想，例如马斯克曾提出利用闲置特斯拉汽车提供“100吉瓦推理”算力，但Xeal的方案是把GPU直接部署在现有EV充电基础设施中，面向都市边缘推理市场。

history.title: Qualcomm will pay Huawei to license its patents for the first time in historic turnaround
history.description: Huawei and Qualcomm sign a multi-year patent cross-license covering 5G and AI, with Qualcomm buying some Huawei US patents.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Qualcomm will pay Huawei for patent rights under a multi-year cross-licensing agreement that highlights both 5G and AI technologies, and will buy some of Huawei’s U.S. patents outright, the firm announced. The joint announcement comes 25 years after Huawei began to pay Qualcomm for patents, a reversal that reportedly has Qualcomm paying for the first time. The agreement also covers compute and networking patents, and the patent purchase will close once it receives regulatory approval.The two companies’ licensing ties date back to 2001, when Huawei, then a Chinese telecom-infrastructure supplier, took a royalty-bearing license to build CDMA network equipment. Qualcomm, which once supplied chips for some Huawei phones, stopped counting royalties from Huawei in its revenue in early 2025.The “broad patent license agreement” allows “cross licenses” and reflects both companies’ commitment to intellectual property rights and to licensing consistent with “fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory (FRAND) principles.” The deal involves no other business cooperation, Huawei said, according to SCMP; this implies no chip sales are involved. The deal follows a settled back royalty dispute in 2020, the U.S. revoking Qualcomm’s license to sell some hardware to Huawei in 2024, and the expiration of Huawei’s license by early 2025.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Qualcomm’s patent purchase covers compute, AI, networking, and “other technologies,” according to the announcement, but the number of patents was not disclosed, nor was any value figure. Each company credits the other’s portfolio. This suggests that the two are trading official recognition of each other’s patents.Huawei says that, with the Qualcomm deal, the total value of its patent-licensing contracts will top $6.9 billion, counting from its first licensing income from Motorola in 2011. Since 2021, it says, its licensing business has brought in more than the company pays for other firms’ patents. In August, the company signed a multi-year Wi-Fi patent cross-license with HP and, as of 2025, the company held 165,000 active granted patents worldwide. It halted royalty payments to Qualcomm in 2018, and its general counsel testified for the FTC about Qualcomm’s licensing terms in the agency’s 2019 antitrust trial against the chipmaker. Huawei can now take some satisfaction in leveling the playing field with Qualcomm.No timetable has been given for closing the patent purchase.
