history.titleZh: 高通将向华为支付专利许可费，历史性逆转首次出现
history.descriptionZh:
高通与华为宣布达成一项多年专利交叉许可协议，高通向华为支付专利权利金，并将直接购买华为部分美国专利。协议突出5G和AI技术，同时还覆盖计算和网络专利。华为表示，该交易不涉及其他业务合作，据南华早报报道，这意味着不涉及芯片销售。专利购买将在获得监管批准后完成，但双方未披露涉及专利数量和交易金额。此次联合声明距华为开始向高通支付专利费约25年，形成明显角色反转：据报道，高通首次成为向华为付费的一方。

从背景看，两家公司的许可关系可追溯至2001年。当时华为还是中国电信基础设施供应商，为制造CDMA网络设备而向高通取得付费专利许可。高通也曾为部分华为手机供应芯片，但从2025年初起，高通不再将来自华为的版税计入营收。此前，双方在2020年解决了一项回授权纠纷；2024年，美国撤销了高通向华为出售部分硬件的许可；到2025年初，华为原有许可到期。此次新协议正是在这些节点之后达成。双方称，这项“广泛专利许可协议”允许交叉许可，体现了两家公司对知识产权以及按照“公平、合理、非歧视（FRAND）原则”进行许可的承诺。

从技术原理看，这类交叉许可的核心是：双方在5G、AI、计算和网络等领域互相授权使用对方的专利技术，从而降低标准必要专利实施中的诉讼风险和许可摩擦。FRAND原则是通信标准专利许可中的关键机制，要求标准必要专利持有人以公平、合理、非歧视的条件授权。高通还将直接购买华为部分美国专利，涉及计算、AI、网络及其他技术，这意味着相关专利所有权将发生转让，而不只是许可使用。其创新性和象征意义在于，华为从历史上的主要被许可方，进一步成为向高通收取专利费并出售专利资产的一方，说明其在5G、AI及相关计算和网络领域的专利组合价值获得认可。需要指出的是，这里的AI技术是专利层面的覆盖，并非具体AI芯片架构、算力、制程或产品合作。

在可比较的数据方面，原文没有披露专利数量、交易金额、支付费率，也没有任何芯片性能、功耗、算力等参数，因此不存在可直接对比的AI芯片性能指标。但可量化的信息包括：双方许可关系始于2001年；华为自2011年从摩托罗拉获得首次许可收入以来，其专利许可合同总价值在本次与高通交易后将超过69亿美元；自2021年以来，华为许可业务收入已超过其向其他公司支付的专利费；截至2025年，华为在全球持有16.5万件有效授权专利。2025年8月，华为还与惠普签署了多年Wi-Fi专利交叉许可。华为也曾通过法院执行专利，例如2024年起诉联发科。华为在2018年停止向高通支付版税，其总法律顾问还在美国联邦贸易委员会2019年针对高通的 antitrust 审判中就高通的许可条款作证。此次协议没有给出专利购买完成的时间表。高通第四财季报告预计下月发布，但其财年在公告前已经结束，因此该交易不会计入这些业绩数字。高通还在上月续签了苹果许可，将在当前延长期结束后于2027年4月1日生效。

从影响和应用场景看，该协议覆盖5G、AI、计算和网络技术，可能影响基站、智能手机、AI计算平台和网络基础设施等领域的专利许可环境。它有助于减少双方在这些领域的专利诉讼摩擦，并推动更多交叉许可和FRAND实践。对华为而言，这意味着专利许可收入和专利地位进一步增强；对高通而言，它获得了华为相关专利授权和部分美国专利资产，但也要承担向华为付费的成本。不过，由于交易明确不涉及其他业务合作，也不涉及芯片销售，因此它不会直接改变高通对华为的芯片供应，也不代表双方在AI芯片产品、AI加速器或算力竞争上的合作。总体上，这一协议更像是一个知识产权格局变化的信号：在5G和AI相关专利领域，华为已从主要支付方转变为高通也需要付费的专利持有方。

history.title: OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design
history.description: OpenAI and Synopsys are developing GPT-Synopsys, a specialized semiconductor-design model that will directly operate Synopsys EDA tools
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter OpenAI and Synopsys have signed a multi-year agreement to jointly develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model optimized for semiconductor design using Synopsys's electronic design automation (EDA) tools. According to the September 30 announcement, the partnership “brings together OpenAI's advanced AI capabilities with Synopsys's industry-leading EDA tools and agentic AI capabilities to revolutionize the design of semiconductors.”Engineers would delegate to agents that run the tools and execute the required processes until the work is ready for review. The companies say this would allow design teams to evaluate more options and deliver more sophisticated chips. Under the preferred partner agreement, OpenAI is licensing Synopsys's tools to develop the model — which will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure — after which the companies will jointly release the product and share revenue. The announcement did not disclose a release date or a pricing structure.AI in chip design so farEngineers use EDA tools to design and verify chips before manufacturing. This multi-step process begins with writing the hardware description in register-transfer level (RTL) code and using synthesis software to convert it into logic gates. Next, physical design tools lay out the circuit elements and route the connections between them. Lastly, designers close timing, verify functionality, and ensure manufacturing compliance before tapeout for fabrication.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Each of these stages requires several iterations — repeatedly running various tools and troubleshooting issues — to balance critical trade-offs: power, performance, and silicon area (PPA). Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens EDA have dominated this market for these tools long before the current AI boom. Given the technology's capabilities, it is only natural that AI has found its way into the chip design process, creating a sort of “silicon designing silicon” loop.In March 2020, Synopsys launched DSO.ai (Design Space Optimization AI), a reinforcement learning tool that explores and learns from previous design optimizations to improve PPA. The company then launched Synopsys.ai Copilot in November 2023 — its first integration of generative AI — through a collaboration with Microsoft, integrating the Azure OpenAI service to provide natural language assistance within its engineering tools. You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond Synopsys debuts Autopilot platform for developing chips autonomously using AI The company’s current direction is Agentic AI, first revealed at the Design Automation Conference in July, where it showed an autonomous verification workflow built on Nvidia's Agent Toolkit and Nemotron 3 Ultra model. On September 28, two days before the OpenAI deal, Synopsys announced its Autopilot platform and AgentEngineer, a portfolio of seven long-horizon agents covering verification, implementation, analog, manufacturing, meshing, combustion, and EMC analysis. The company reported more than 50 engagements, with availability planned for late 2026.As detailed in our State of agentic AI in chip design tools roadmap, the move to agentic AI is not exclusive to Synopsys; Cadence and Siemens are also pitching autonomous design agents. Meanwhile, OpenAI, in collaboration with Broadcom, unveiled Jalapeño in June, the company’s first custom inference accelerator. OpenAI said the accelerator's design and optimization process leaned heavily on its AI models, allowing it to go from initial design to tape-out in just nine months. Now, GPT-Synopsys turns that internal experiment into a product.GPT-SynopsysAccording to the announcement, GPT-Synopsys will combine OpenAI's frontier models with Synopsys’s EDA software and domain expertise, allowing the model to reason about chip design and verification and operate Synopsys tools directly. Engineers would hand the model objectives such as PPA optimization, timing, and verification closure, while the agents run the tools, interpret the results, implement changes, and iterate toward verified outcomes for an engineer to review.In other words, the model would be capable of making engineering judgments involved in using Synopsys software. The companies describe it as learning to operate the tools like an expert engineer, interpreting their outputs and using the results to guide further changes. This is the proposed specialization that takes the model beyond connecting a general-purpose model to a set of tools.Synopsys’s EDA engines would perform the calculations and checks, with the model interpreting results and the agent software managing execution. GPT-Synopsys will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and is intended to integrate with Synopsys.ai and Autopilot, as well as work with customers’ own agent harnesses. Autopilot already provides services such as memory and governance. What to read next Amazon and Synopsys ink multi-year billion-dollar deal in multi-year IP agreement to accelerate AI chip design efforts ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs Synopsys says early technology engagements are underway with leading semiconductor customers, but didn't name any. The immediate audience is professional semiconductor-design teams, with companies developing their own custom silicon also likely to use it. Although the announcement covers semiconductor design generally, OpenAI has a particular interest in improving the hardware that runs its models. “By helping them build better chips, we can build better AI and bring it to more people,” said Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder. Whether the service also makes advanced design more accessible to smaller teams will depend on pricing and the expertise still required to supervise it.Questions and concernsThe recent announcement leaves a couple of questions and concerns unaddressed. First, hosting the model on OpenAI infrastructure raises concerns about how confidential designs are handled. The companies say customer data will be excluded from model training, encrypted at rest and in transit, and governed by configurable retention, audit, and permission controls. However, the release does not identify hosting regions or default retention periods. It also provides no contractual terms for ownership of generated outputs, use of third-party licensed design IP, or indemnities. The service's terms will likely address these questions.Another question is the practical economics for users. The industry has realized that handing over everything to AI doesn't always result in cost savings, at least for now. Sometimes the reverse is the case. Earlier this year, Uber’s CTO and an Nvidia executive said AI was more expensive than human workers, although many companies are reportedly fine with the extra cost. For GPT-Synopsys, advanced engineering reasoning and faster design-to-tapeout could justify the service, but model calls, EDA runs, integration, and human review all consume resources. The announcement did not include a pricing structure. It also didn't specify a launch date.Meanwhile, Synopsys’s main rival Cadence launched its ChipStack AI Super Agent in February for front-end design and verification, built on frontier LLMs. In April, the company announced a collaboration with Google to optimize ChipStack with Gemini on Google Cloud. At Computex, it extended ChipStack to what it calls Level-5 autonomy, powered by Nvidia's Nemotron models, with early access expected in the second half of 2026. The main difference is that while ChipStack is Cadence’s own agent software running on other companies’ general-purpose models, GPT-Synopsys will be an OpenAI model specifically trained to operate Synopsys’s tools.

history.titleZh: OpenAI与新思科技合作打造“GPT-Synopsys”以实现自主芯片设计
history.descriptionZh:
OpenAI与Synopsys于9月30日宣布签署多年协议，将联合开发GPT-Synopsys。这是一个面向半导体设计的专用模型，基于Synopsys的电子设计自动化（EDA）工具优化。双方称，该合作把OpenAI的先进AI能力与Synopsys行业领先的EDA工具及智能体AI能力结合，目标是革新芯片设计。按照“优先合作伙伴协议”，OpenAI获授权使用Synopsys工具来开发模型，模型将运行在OpenAI托管的基础设施上；之后双方将联合发布产品并分享收入。公告未披露发布日期和定价结构。

背景方面，工程师使用EDA工具在制造前设计和验证芯片。流程从编写寄存器传输级（RTL）硬件描述开始，用综合软件转换为逻辑门；随后物理设计工具布局电路元件并布线；最后设计人员完成时序收敛、功能验证和制造合规检查，再送交流片。每个阶段都需要多轮迭代，反复运行各类工具并排查问题，以平衡功耗、性能和硅面积（PPA）等关键取舍。Synopsys、Cadence和Siemens EDA在AI热潮之前就长期主导这一市场。AI进入芯片设计后，形成了某种“硅设计硅”的循环。Synopsys早在2020年3月推出DSO.ai，用强化学习探索并学习既往设计优化，以改善PPA；2023年11月又与微软合作推出Synopsys.ai Copilot，首次集成生成式AI，通过Azure OpenAI服务在工程工具内提供自然语言辅助。其当前方向是智能体AI：7月在Design Automation Conference上展示了基于Nvidia Agent Toolkit和Nemotron 3 Ultra模型的自主验证工作流；9月28日，即OpenAI交易前两天，Synopsys发布Autopilot平台和AgentEngineer，包含七个长周期智能体，覆盖验证、实现、模拟、制造、网格划分、燃烧和EMC分析，已报告超过50个合作项目，计划2026年底可用。Cadence和Siemens也在推出自主设计智能体。OpenAI则与Broadcom合作，在6月发布Jalapeño，这是其首个定制推理加速器；OpenAI称该加速器的设计和优化过程大量依赖其AI模型，从初始设计到流片仅用9个月。GPT-Synopsys则是把这一内部实验转化为产品。

技术原理上，GPT-Synopsys将OpenAI的前沿模型与Synopsys的EDA软件及领域专业知识结合，使模型能够推理芯片设计与验证，并直接操作Synopsys工具。工程师可向模型提交PPA优化、时序收敛、验证收敛等目标，由智能体运行工具、解读结果、实施修改并迭代，直到形成可供工程师审核的已验证结果。换言之，模型要像专家工程师一样操作工具、理解输出，并据此指导后续修改，而不仅是把通用模型连接到一组工具上。Synopsys的EDA引擎负责计算和检查，模型解读结果，智能体软件管理执行。GPT-Synopsys将运行在OpenAI托管的基础设施上，计划集成到Synopsys.ai和Autopilot，也可与客户自有的智能体框架配合。Autopilot已提供记忆和治理等服务。Synopsys称已与领先半导体客户开展早期技术合作，但未点名。其直接受众是专业半导体设计团队，开发自研芯片的公司也可能使用。OpenAI尤其关注改进运行其模型的硬件。OpenAI总裁兼联合创始人Greg Brockman表示：“通过帮助他们造更好的芯片，我们可以造更好的AI，并把它带给更多人。”该服务是否能让小团队也更容易使用先进设计，将取决于定价以及仍需人类监督的专业能力。

问题和担忧方面，首先，将模型托管在OpenAI基础设施上，引发机密设计如何处理的担忧。双方称客户数据将被排除在模型训练之外，静态和传输中加密，并受可配置的保留、审计和权限控制约束；但发布信息未说明托管区域或默认保留期，也没有关于生成输出所有权、第三方授权设计IP使用或赔偿的合同条款。服务条款可能会回应这些问题。其次是用户的实际经济性。业界已意识到，把所有事情交给AI并不总能节省成本，至少目前如此，有时反而更贵。今年早些时候，Uber首席技术官和一位Nvidia高管称AI比人类员工更贵，尽管据报道许多公司接受这种额外成本。对GPT-Synopsys而言，高级工程推理和更快设计到流片可能证明其价值，但模型调用、EDA运行、集成和人工审核都会消耗资源。公告未包含定价结构，也未指定上市日期。竞争方面，Synopsys主要对手Cadence在2月推出ChipStack AI Super Agent，用于前端设计与验证，基于前沿LLM；4月宣布与Google合作，在Google Cloud上用Gemini优化ChipStack；在Computex上将其扩展到所谓Level-5自主性，由Nvidia Nemotron模型驱动，预计2026年下半年早期访问。关键区别在于：ChipStack是Cadence自己的智能体软件，运行在其他公司的通用模型上；GPT-Synopsys则是OpenAI专门训练来操作Synopsys工具的模型。

history.title: Elon Musk pledges SpaceXSI rebrand after Trump's executive order to use 'Super Intelligence' moniker
history.description: Elon Musk says he plans to rename SpaceXAI as SpaceXSI to reflect the new "Super Intelligence" moniker adopted in President Trump's executive order
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk has confirmed that SpaceXAI will change its name to SpaceXSI, to reflect the new moniker “Super Intelligence” coined by President Trump as a replacement for “Artificial Intelligence.” In an X post on September 4, Musk wrote, “Yes, we will make that change,” in response to an X user’s question about renaming the AI company. Musk had earlier posted, “No more AI. SI. It’s better,” following up the post with a photo of the cover page of Nick Bostrom's book, “Superintelligence.”President Donald Trump signed the executive order to officially rebrand “Artificial Intelligence” to “Super Intelligence” on September 29, 2026, during a high-level technology summit at the White House dubbed “Super Intelligence Luncheon.” The administration argued that “artificial” implies something fake and that “super intelligence” better captures the technology's true scale and potential. Several Federal agencies have already implemented the rebrand.Six days after the summit, President Trump formally launched the “Super Intelligence Force” (SIF) through a presidential mandate and public announcement via Truth Social on Sunday, October 4, following up on his earlier promise to launch a force that will “cherish” the technology and “help it grow.” The Force will report directly to the White House and will oversee domestic AI policy, ensure American AI dominance over global rivals like China, and interface directly with the private tech sector.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Regarding the rebrand, it is unclear how the numerous American AI companies with “AI” in their names and products intend to proceed. Furthermore, the total number of registered .ai domains has officially surpassed 1 million globally. Registrations had reportedly generated an estimated $96.4 million for the 2026 budget of Antigua — a tiny Caribbean island nation with “.ai” as its country-code top-level domain — accounting for nearly half of total government revenue.Following the announcement, speculators are frantically buying up .si domains, often registering look-alike domains mirroring existing .ai sites. Musk has yet to implement the “SI” nomenclature across his companies, with the X.ai domain still featuring “AI” and “Artificial Intelligence” in all copies sitewide, as of this report. history.titleZh: Elon Musk pledges SpaceXSI rebrand after Trump's executive order to use 'Super Intelligence' moniker
history.descriptionZh:
据 Tom's Hardware 报道，埃隆·马斯克已确认 SpaceXAI 将更名为 SpaceXSI，以配合美国总统特朗普提出的新术语“Super Intelligence”（超级智能），用来取代“Artificial Intelligence”（人工智能）。9月4日，马斯克在 X 上回应网友关于更名的提问时写道“是的，我们会改”，并在此前发帖称“不要再叫 AI 了，叫 SI，更好”，还附上尼克·博斯特罗姆《超级智能》一书封面。

背景上，特朗普于2026年9月29日在白宫一场名为“Super Intelligence Luncheon”的高级别科技峰会上签署行政命令，正式将“Artificial Intelligence”重新命名为“Super Intelligence”。其政府认为“artificial”暗示虚假，而“super intelligence”更能体现这项技术的真实规模和潜力。多个联邦机构已开始执行这一更名。

六天后，即10月4日星期日，特朗普通过总统授权和 Truth Social 公开宣布正式启动“Super Intelligence Force”（SIF，超级智能部队/力量）。该机构直接向白宫汇报，负责监督美国国内AI政策，确保美国在全球AI竞争中相对于中国等对手的主导地位，并直接与私营科技部门对接。此前他曾承诺建立一支“珍视”该技术并“帮助其成长”的力量。

报道指出，围绕更名仍存在不确定性：大量名称或产品中含有“AI”的美国AI公司打算如何应对尚不清楚。同时，全球注册的 .ai 域名总数已正式超过100万个；这些注册为加勒比小岛国安提瓜2026年预算带来约9640万美元收入，占其政府总收入近一半，因为 .ai 是安提瓜的国家代码顶级域名。更名消息宣布后，投机者疯狂抢购 .si 域名，常注册与现有 .ai 网站相似的仿冒域名。马斯克尚未在其公司全面实施“SI”命名：截至报道时，X.ai 域名及全站文案仍使用“AI”和“Artificial Intelligence”。

核心上，此事并非新的AI技术性能发布，也没有芯片、模型参数或基准数据披露。其“创新”主要在于术语、品牌和政策框架重构：用“超级智能”替代“人工智能”，并设立白宫直属的 SIF 来统筹国内AI政策、国际竞争和私营部门协调。影响可能波及企业品牌与域名策略、政府文件用语、AI产业监管，以及 .ai/.si 域名生态；但实际执行、企业跟进程度和技术含义仍有待观察。

history.content: Google may be expanding its “Call for Me” AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a “Gemini Calling” introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include “Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late” and “Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner.”Based on those examples, even with this expansion, Gemini would likely be limited to basic, text message-like calls. While Google’s AI might not automate an entire catch-up phone call with your relatives, it could deliver quick messages to people who prefer a phone call, miss texts often, or even still have a landline phone.Android Authority also says it found “granular permissions” for Gemini actions in individual apps, including what appear to be settings for phone call permissions. These settings would allow users to pick and choose which app capabilities they want to allow Gemini to access, potentially giving users an option to opt out of receiving incoming automated calls from Gemini. However, as Android Authority notes, it’s also possible Google might not publicly release this expansion or the granular Gemini app settings.

history.titleZh: Gemini为我通话可能会告诉你妈妈你要迟到了
history.descriptionZh:
根据 Android Authority 的 APK 拆解，Google 可能正在把其“Call for Me”AI 功能从商务通话扩展到个人通讯，让用户通过 Gemini 向朋友和家人发送电话消息。拆解中出现了名为“Gemini Calling”的介绍页面，示例指令包括“打电话给妈妈，告诉她我会迟到 15 分钟”和“打电话给 John，问他是否来吃晚饭”。这表明 Gemini 可能获得发起电话呼叫并传递简短信息的能力。

背景上，Call for Me 原本更多与商务或事务性通话相关，而新线索显示 Google 想把它用于亲友之间的短信式沟通。所谓 APK 拆解，是指从 Android 应用安装包中提前发现尚未正式发布的功能，因此目前不能确认该功能一定会上线。

技术原理上，这类功能通常由 Gemini 解析用户的自然语言指令，提取联系人、通话目的和要传达的内容，再通过电话网络自动拨号，并以合成语音或类似交互式语音的方式把信息告诉对方。创新点不只是“AI 打电话”，还包括将复杂的语音助手能力压缩到简单、可靠、可重复的短消息场景。根据示例，它很可能不会自动完成一次完整的叙旧电话，而是像“语音短信”一样传递具体信息。

报道还提到，拆解中发现了 Gemini 在单个应用中的“细粒度权限”设置，包括电话通话权限。这意味着用户可能可以逐项选择允许 Gemini 访问哪些应用能力，甚至可以选择不接收 Gemini 自动打来的电话。这有助于缓解隐私、骚扰和自动化通话方面的担忧。

性能参数方面，目前没有延迟、通话成功率、支持机型、语言范围或正式发布时间等数据。与现有商务通话场景相比，这次扩展的主要变化是从商业用途走向个人通讯，但能力边界仍可能局限于基础消息传递。其潜在应用包括：给更爱接电话、经常漏看短信、甚至仍在使用座机的人快速传话，例如通知迟到、确认晚餐、提醒事项等。

不过，Android Authority 也指出，Google 可能不会公开发布这一扩展或细粒度权限设置。因此，目前这仍属于 APK 线索层面的可能性，而非正式产品发布。若最终落地，它可能让 Gemini 成为电话与短信之间的 AI 中介，但也会引发对自动来电、隐私授权和真实通话体验的讨论。
